text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000174 bills 99215 at several times the expected rate in every complexity tier, but the limited records returned mostly support the billed level, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not confined to sicker patients: the by-complexity table shows the provider's 99215 share running roughly three times the all-provider share even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions (e.g., C0081769, C0081968, C0082077), and the coding mix is also heavily weighted toward 99214, which is consistent with upward drift rather than a uniquely complex panel. Against that, most of the 19 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM, including low-complexity claim C0082074, and the 2 unsupported claims (C0082021, C0082040) are too few to separate from documentation noise, though they exceed the comparison rate. The documentation may not be fully reliable: 6 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed have no lab or test on the claim, the repeated-time and problem-list signals are present, and without an audit trail cloned or templated notes cannot be ruled out. A reviewer should first pull additional charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, especially repeat patients such as M0034588, and check whether their MDM narratives are patient-specific rather than templated."}
